displayName: Disable or Modify Tools: Clear Linux or Mac System Logs

tests.name: rm -rf
tests.description: Delete system and audit logs

tests.name: rm -rf
tests.description: Delete messages and security logs

tests.name: Delete log files using built-in log utility
tests.description: This test deletes main log datastore, inflight log data, time-to-live data(TTL), fault and error content

tests.name: Truncate system log files via truncate utility
tests.description: This test truncates the system log files using the truncate utility with (-s 0) parameter which sets file size to zero, thus emptying the file content

tests.name: Truncate system log files via truncate utility (freebsd)
tests.description: This test truncates the system log files using the truncate utility with (-s 0 or --size=0) parameter which sets file size to zero, thus emptying the file content

tests.name: Delete log files via cat utility by appending /dev/null or /dev/zero
tests.description: The first sub-test truncates the log file to zero bytes via /dev/null and the second sub-test fills the log file with null bytes(zeroes) via /dev/zero, using cat utility

tests.name: Delete log files via cat utility by appending /dev/null or /dev/zero (freebsd)
tests.description: The first sub-test truncates the log file to zero bytes via /dev/null and the second sub-test fills the log file with null bytes(zeroes) via /dev/zero, using cat utility

tests.name: System log file deletion via find utility
tests.description: This test finds and deletes the system log files within /var/log/ directory using various executions(rm, shred, unlink)

tests.name: Overwrite macOS system log via echo utility
tests.description: This test overwrites the contents of system log file with an empty string using echo utility

tests.name: Overwrite FreeBSD system log via echo utility
tests.description: This test overwrites the contents of system log file with an empty string using echo utility

tests.name: Real-time system log clearance/deletion
tests.description: This test reads real-time system log file and writes empty string to it, thus clearing the log file without tampering with the logging process

tests.name: Delete system log files via unlink utility
tests.description: This test deletes the system log file using unlink utility

tests.name: Delete system log files via unlink utility (freebsd)
tests.description: This test deletes the messages log file using unlink utility

tests.name: Delete system log files using shred utility
tests.description: This test overwrites the contents of the log file with zero bytes(-z) using three passes(-n 3) of data, and then delete the file(-u) securely

tests.name: Delete system log files using srm utility
tests.description:
This test securely deletes the system log files individually and recursively using the srm utility.
Install srm using Homebrew with the command: brew install khell/homebrew-srm/srm
Refer: https://github.com/khell/homebrew-srm/issues/1 for installation

tests.name: Delete system log files using OSAScript
tests.description: This test deletes the system log file using osascript via "do shell script"(sh/bash by default) which in-turn spawns rm utility, requires admin privileges

tests.name: Delete system log files using Applescript
tests.description:
This test deletes the system log file using applescript using osascript via Finder application
Note: The user may be prompted to grant access to the Finder application before the command can be executed successfully as part of TCC(Transparency, Consent, and Control) Framework.
Refer: https://www.rainforestqa.com/blog/macos-tcc-db-deep-dive

tests.name: Delete system journal logs via rm and journalctl utilities
tests.description: The first sub-test deletes the journal files using rm utility in the "/var/log/journal/" directory and the second sub-test clears the journal by modifiying time period of logs that should be retained to zero.

tests.name: Overwrite Linux Mail Spool
tests.description: This test overwrites the Linux mail spool of a specified user. This technique was used by threat actor Rocke during the exploitation of Linux web servers.

tests.name: Overwrite Linux Log
tests.description: This test overwrites the specified log. This technique was used by threat actor Rocke during the exploitation of Linux web servers.
